purpose: Object geometry and orientation-equivalence for the POSE_METRIC_CLOSURE_V1 evaluation only.

relationship_to_existing_registry.why_separate: the existing registry's sha256 is pinned in 62 files across 198 places. Editing it to mark wood's symmetry FROZEN would rewrite the provenance of every prior experiment. This contract is additive: it governs this evaluation and nothing else.

orientation_definition.why_180_is_equivalent: both objects are rectangular cuboids, so a half turn about the vertical axis maps the object onto itself
orientation_definition.why_90_is_not: the footprints are rectangular, and a quarter turn changes which face the forks enter. It is a different pose for the task, not a symmetry.
orientation_definition.yaw_metric: yaw error is evaluated modulo 180, folded into 0..90 degrees

plastic_standard_110x130x11.equivalence_basis: rectangular cuboid; the half turn is an exact geometric symmetry of the shape

wood_small_80x59x14.equivalence_basis: declared benchmark/operational long-axis equivalence; not claimed as verified full visual symmetry

measured_support.footprint: 0.80 x 0.59 m rectangular, so 90 and 270 are excluded by geometry alone
measured_support.unverified: the opposite fork-entry face is never observed in any frame, and one block carries an IPPC stamp, so the object is visually asymmetric under 180 degrees even though it is geometrically symmetric

usage.rule: the pose evaluation must be given this path explicitly. It never falls back to the historical evaluator contract, and the two are never silently merged.
usage.recorded_in_results: the sha256 of this file is written into every pose evaluation result produced under this track
